Project overview

A completed turn-based macOS experiment

Local Voice Assistant was a single-user macOS experiment that connected microphone input, local transcription, a local language model, and speech playback in one turn-based loop. Pressing Return started recording; pressing it again ended the utterance.

The terminal printed the recognized speech and the assistant response, then played the synthesized reply. An earlier retained browser/server experiment explored a lower-latency direction; the archived formal entrypoint is a local command-line application.

Recorded implementation

Local model runtimes joined by a Python CLI

The archived CLI recorded 16 kHz mono audio with sounddevice and wrote temporary audio under the project directory. mlx-whisper transcribed it locally with a Whisper small model. llama-cpp-python then ran a local Qwen2.5-3B GGUF model using the system instruction and current utterance.

MLX-Audio/Kokoro synthesized the reply. The app selected a Mandarin voice when Chinese characters appeared and an English voice otherwise, then played the generated audio with afplay. If Kokoro failed, it fell back to macOS say.

The inference path ran locally once model assets were available; setup could download those assets when needed. This one-turn experiment did not implement conversation history, durable memory, voice activity detection, interruption handling, or realtime audio streaming.

One interaction turn

Record, transcribe, respond, play

  1. 01

    Start recording

    Pressing Return in the terminal started recording from the microphone.

  2. 02

    Stop recording

    Pressing Return again finished the utterance and saved temporary local audio.

  3. 03

    Transcribe and respond

    Local Whisper produced text, then the local Qwen model received that utterance and returned a concise reply.

  4. 04

    Synthesize and play

    Kokoro produced an English or Mandarin spoken response for macOS playback; say was available if synthesis failed.
